dave_cust: Hey - our customers started seeing 502/504s to the hosted API around 08:12 PDT. This looks like TLS failures / handshake timeouts from our side. Sample from a failing request: 

curl -v https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer ***'
* About to connect() to api.redwood-inference.com port 443 (#0)
*   Trying 52.23.11.7... 
* connect to 52.23.11.7 port 443 failed: Operation timed out
* Failed to connect to api.redwood-inference.com port 443: Operation timed out
* Closing connection 0
curl: (7) Failed to connect

Also tried openssl s_client: 
```
openssl s_client -connect api.redwood-inference.com:443 -servername api.redwood-inference.com -timeout 5
CONNECTED(00000003)
139831...: TLS handshake timeout
---
no peer certificate
---
```

Any hotfix we can do? Customers are escalating.

alice_support: Thanks, Dave. Can you paste a few request IDs and the region (we're assuming us-west-2 from the IP above)? Any time correlation with deploys or cert changes? Also, do you see consistent failures from multiple customer networks or only some ISPs?

dave_cust: Request IDs: req_01HXYZZA1, req_01HXYZZA2. Seeing it from multiple customer networks (at least two different ASNs). Not limited to one ISP. We noticed it coincided with a cert rotation notification in our logs ~08:10 UTC.

deploy-bot: cert-rotation: completed cert rotation for api.redwood-inference.com at 2026-03-15T08:10:05Z by rollout/cert-2026-03-15

bob_sre: I'm seeing a spike in 502/504 from the edge mesh starting 08:11 UTC. Our edge logs show upstream connect timeouts to certain backend IPs. Also seeing DNS anomalies where some resolvers return an older A record list while others return the new set. Looks like a DNS propagation/caching mismatch post-rotation.

carol_eng: Adding diagnostic steps to reproduce for us: 
1) dig +short api.redwood-inference.com @8.8.8.8\2) dig +noall +answer api.redwood-inference.com @<customer-resolver>\3) curl -v --resolve api.redwood-inference.com:443:<ip> https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/health\n
Example output I got: 
```
$ dig +noall +answer api.redwood-inference.com @1.1.1.1\api.redwood-inference.com.  300 IN A 52.23.11.7\api.redwood-inference.com.  300 IN A 18.205.93.2
```
But some stale resolvers still had 204.15.99.8 which is an older pool we decommissioned last week. That older pool wasn't fully rotated with the new cert chain (we issued an ECDSA-only cert), so connections to 204.15.99.8 hit nodes that present the old chain or fail OCSP. That can show up as handshake timeouts depending on client behavior.

alice_support: If that's the case, immediate mitigations: 
- Add a short-term routing fallback so clients that fail regionally are routed to the global pool (we can flip to global routing policy).
- Push an emergency DNS cache flush (internal resolvers + Cloud DNS TTL lowering) and mark the old IPs as draining in the load balancer.
- As a customer workaround, ask them to `dig +trace` and try hitting the new IPs with `--resolve` to verify connectivity.

bob_sre: I'm going to mark IPs 204.15.99.8 and 204.15.99.9 as draining and add them to the quarantine list so they stop getting traffic from the public LB. Will also set DNS TTL to 30s for the next 10 minutes to accelerate propagation.

carol_eng: Root cause theory: the cert we rotated to is ECDSA-only and some legacy edge hosts hadn't picked up the new intermediate (or were still running an older OpenSSL build that failed an ECDSA-only handshake in combination with the old ALPN ordering). Combined with DNS cache staleness that sent traffic to those hosts -> handshake failures/timeouts. Two simultaneous failures (cert chain mismatch + DNS returning decommissioned IPs).

Steps we used to reproduce locally: 
```
dig +trace api.redwood-inference.com
dig @<customer-resolver> api.redwood-inference.com +noall +answer
openssl s_client -connect 204.15.99.8:443 -servername api.redwood-inference.com -tlsextdebug -status
```
Example of the failure output: 
```
OCSP response: no response sent
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
SSL handshake has read 0 bytes and written 396 bytes
```

alice_support: Carol, do we have a quick option to re-issue a cert with an RSA chain cross-signed so older edge nodes will accept it? Or replace the chain on the decommissioned pool?

carol_eng: We can either: 
- re-issue a cert with an RSA-compatible chain (fast, few minutes), or 
- force a faster config push to the remaining old nodes to ensure they show the new chain (riskier).
Given customer impact, I'll request an emergency RSA cross-signed cert now. Also asking network to flush any authoritative resolver caches for the old A records.

bob_sre: Done: set LB draining on 204.15.99.8/9 and lowered DNS TTL to 30. Also pushed a cache purge request to the authoritative provider. Beginning rollout of temporary firewall rule to prevent clients from being routed to the old pool IPs.

dave_cust: Thanks. I asked our customers to try `curl --resolve api.redwood-inference.com:443:52.23.11.7 https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/health` and they got 200. One of them confirmed cleared DNS cache and now working. But a few corporate networks still see failures (likely internal resolver caching).

carol_eng: Emergency cert issued (RSA cross-signed) and rolled into the global edge at 08:23 UTC. Confirming via openssl: 
```
openssl s_client -connect api.redwood-inference.com:443 -servername api.redwood-inference.com 
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=api.redwood-inference.com
 1 s:/CN=Redwood-Intermediate (RSA)
---
SSL handshake ok
```

bob_sre: Monitoring metrics: 5xx rate dropped back to baseline by 08:30 UTC after draining old IPs and cert update. Still seeing a few stragglers from corporate resolvers that have long caches. We'll follow up with support templates for customers to clear DNS or use the fallback.

alice_support: Creating a follow-up incident ticket to document: cert rotation produced ECDSA-only chain, decommissioned IPs still cached in some resolvers -> disconnects/handshake timeouts. Actions taken: drain old IPs, lower TTL, issue RSA cross-signed cert, purge caches. Recommend future rotations include RSA-compatible chain for 48 hours after decommission window.

dave_cust: Appreciate the quick response. Please send the mitigation steps I can forward to affected customers (sample curl commands + recommended clear-cache steps).

alice_support: Will post a short customer-facing snippet in the ticket and dm you. Closing this thread once ticket is created. :white_check_mark:
